586f23f8-81a9-4a68-93b3-f3e423ad4a30.one_liner: A macro strategist's tour through Fed politics, AI capex financing, and the Treasury's new long-end buyback program touches directly on rates/duration positioning even though it's framed as broad macro commentary.
586f23f8-81a9-4a68-93b3-f3e423ad4a30.recap: JST Advisors' John Turek discusses the Warsh Fed, comparing him to ECB's Lagarde as an 'owl' figure rather than a strong hawk/dove, someone solving for political optimization rather than leading with a fixed framework -- a stance the market punished after July's press conference produced a bear steepening. Turek sees the US economy driven increasingly by AI capex rather than consumption, arguing hyperscalers are spending from a fear of falling behind (a left-tail-avoidance motive) more than a pure right-tail bet, implying capex could keep rising through 2027 -- but a capex bust, if it comes, would be severe given the scale involved. He explains the sharp back-end selloff (30yr near decade highs) as driven by hyperscalers exhausting free cash flow and turning to debt markets just as global savings (increasingly only East Asian households) fail to keep pace with surging investment demand. He then covers the US Treasury's newly expanded long-end buyback program, arguing it's less about market dysfunction and more a level-targeting move akin to prior FX interventions (dollar-yen, the FX swap facility), raising the risk that funding buybacks via bill issuance could eventually force the Fed to restart reserve management purchases -- effectively QE. He also flags a hawkish ECB reaction function, German fiscal deterioration and rising AFD support, and a durable Iran/Strait of Hormuz standoff keeping refined product prices elevated and inflation risk skewed higher.
terms: OIS -- Overnight Index Swap, a derivative referencing the compounded overnight rate, used as a rates benchmark
RMP -- Reserve Management Purchases, Fed asset purchases used to manage bank reserve levels distinct from QE
PCE -- Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge
ECI -- Employment Cost Index, a wage/compensation cost measure used by the Fed as a preferred wage tracker
